reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–31 of the combined Higher Level scheme (cover, notes, the Paper 1 scale table on page 4, the summary of allocations on page 5, annotation palette, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note, and the Paper 2 title page). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The 2022 paper was adjusted for COVID-19 (220 marks): candidates answer any four of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any two of Q7–10 (50 marks each), so 380 marks are offered and 220 count. Every question is retained.

43 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 5. Shared scales keep their parts together: Q1(c)(i)–(ii) 15D, Q7(a)–(b) 10D, Q7(f)(i)–(ii) 5C, Q8(a)–(b) 15D and Q10(c)(i)–(ii) 10C.

All 43 units were already authored and shipping. Prompts are restored from the paper (several had lost superscripts, fractions and their preamble). Q3(b), Q6(b) and Q8(e) carried marking points garbled by the scheme text layer (interleaved columns, a stacked 15/2 read as “( )/2 15”); they are re-quoted line by line and labelled with their scheme band. Topics are corrected as metadata; all IDs are kept.
The question booklet is LC003ALP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions, which match the printed scheme page numbers.

cards.stem: If we learn a skill, and then don’t practise it, how well we can do it usually decreases over time. For example, if you learn to play the guitar, and then don’t play the guitar for a number of months, you will probably not be as good at playing the guitar the first time you try it again. This effect can be modelled by the following equation: A = B(t + 1)^c, where A is a measure of how well the skill can be done at a certain time (t = 0); B is a measure of how well the skill can be done t months later, without practising; c is a constant; and A, B, c, t ∈ ℝ.
cards.questionText: Write c in terms of log₁₀ A, log₁₀ B, and log₁₀(t + 1).
